activity.title: 🐦 Parrot (YC F25) Launched the TikTok for Learning Any Language You Want.

Parrot just crossed 100,000 downloads on the App Store in under 8 months. That’s the equivalent of filling Wembley Stadium at full capacity with people who chose to learn Spanish with Parrot. 🇬🇧🦜 More languages coming soon ;) What’s even crazier is how they found us. From Apple’s own analytics: 1. 85.3% of our downloads (94,295 people) came from App Store Search 2. And we don’t rank for “learn Spanish,” “language learning,” or any major keyword yet... 3. Meaning, the overwhelming majority of people typed “Parrot” directly into the search bar People aren’t stumbling onto Parrot. They’re looking for it by name. That’s real brand pull. That’s movement-level awareness. And it’s all before we’ve even scratched the surface of ASO or SEO, or LLM SEO. Onwards. 🦜💙 Parrot (YC F25) ...more ...more

Parrot (YC F25) went from $0 → $79K MRR in just 8.5 months. With 3,000+ active trials and 7,300+ customers, we’ll cross $1M ARR in the next few days. As software becomes easier to build, the real competitive edge shifts to distribution, viral loops, and brand. We launched Parrot’s subscription in March, fully bootstrapped, and grew our creator network from 8 creators to 39 amazing creators producing content for Parrot. The inflection point hit in October when we expanded our creator network, and things have been compounding ever since. What's a growth strategy that you've been gatekeeping? ...more ...more
Huge thank you to Dasha and Forbes for featuring Parrot and sharing our story. Grateful to be highlighted alongside so many incredible founders and companies! ...more

We entered YC with $16K MRR. 100% bootstrapped. Today, we’re at $75K MRR, a 4.7× increase in just 6 weeks ( and $1.1M in annualized run rate) and on track to double before the end of the year. It’s been wild watching Parrot evolve from a scrappy experiment into a product people genuinely love using daily. Every day, new users tell us the same thing: “It doesn’t feel like I’m studying. I’m just scrolling.” That’s exactly the point. We’re building the first language app designed for the way people actually spend time on their phones, swiping through short, entertaining videos. Except this time, it’s productive scrolling. We’re just getting started. The retention is improving, the love is real, and the growth is compounding. Super excited to keep talking to users and making Parrot 100x better. ...more ...more

It’s a dream come true to get into YC but the best part of it all is getting to work on a product I strongly believe in. Language learning shouldn’t be just a mindless game, it can be fun while also being effective. Every learner feedback call is confirmation that we are moving in the right direction and it’s the best part of every day for me. I can’t wait to see what the future holds for Parrot! ...more

“Why would we compete with a $14B giant?” “How did Duolingo make hundreds of millions and still get no one fluent?” “Another language app? Isn’t there thousands of those?” Those were my exact questions when my co-founder Erik Dahl told me he wanted to build another language app. At first, I wasn’t convinced. But after working with Erik on a few startups, I knew one thing about him: if he’s obsessed with an idea, it’s probably worth exploring. Then Julia Hudea joined, we met in a university entrepreneurship class at The University of British Columbia . We’d both worked on things that could’ve worked but didn’t matter to us. This one did. Before writing any code, we: 1. Downloaded 52 language learning apps and used every single one for a few hours. 2. Interviewed 65 language learners across Reddit, Discord, and our circles. 3. Found the comprehensible input method, the most research-backed approach to learning a language (listen first, speak later). We built a simple MVP, just a video player with captions, and took it to students. 60% paid for early access. That moment flipped my skepticism into conviction. Fast forward, Parrot is now growing super fast, joined Y Combinator 's Fall 2025 batch, and some learners spending 1hr+ on the app. What started as doubt turned into a mission: to connect people by breaking down language barriers. To make learning a language feel as natural and addictive as scrolling TikTok . ...more ...more
Check out what we're doing at Parrot!

TL;DR Apple just gave us the best marketing campaign we could ask for. They showed the world that cross-language connection matters - and we’re here for the people who want to do it without training wheels. Apple just announced real-time translation through AirPods. It’s an incredible leap forward in tech - the kind of innovation that inspires us at Parrot. But here’s what it doesn’t do: It doesn’t help you really understand native speakers. It doesn’t help you respond with confidence. It doesn’t make you fluent - it makes you dependent. And that’s why I’m more excited than ever about what we’re building. At Parrot (YC F25) , we help people actually acquire languages - not just translate it. Because fluency isn’t just about survival. It’s about connection. Culture. Confidence. Being able to feel what someone’s saying - not just hear it filtered through an algorithm. Apple’s innovation is a rising tide. It will make the world more curious, more connected, more multilingual. And we’re here for the people who see that future and say: 🦜 “I want to speak the language myself.” ...more ...more

I came back from my first work conference with exactly one photo, and it is of the hotel room 🤦‍♀️ That's because SupeTank isn't a normal conference. There's no booth to stand behind, you pitch directly to sitting superintendents. There was no time for photos. It makes me extremely happy to say that Socra Education 's mission and product resonated. We got an overwhelming number of yeses when we asked whether superintendents would refer us to their teams for a pilot 🚀 One superintendent even told us Socra was exactly the product he came all the way to see! Superintendents have a thankless job, and it's an especially hard one right now. That they still make time to engage with founders building toward meeting their learners' needs says everything about why they do this work. The other half of it was the founders. It's not very often I'm surrounded by people who have made education their life's work and who have such a clear vision for where it should head. I'll inevitably miss names here, but thank you to Dr Jasminka Criley, MD, FACP, FHM , Lemi-Ola Erinkitola , Stephanie (Batory) Brown, Aman Sahota , Stuart Criley , and Demetra Mallios for all the conversations. And thank you to Tiffany Law for convincing me we are not too early to get value out of this, Whitney Ballantine , Doug Roberts , and the rest of the Institute for Education Innovation team for bringing it all together.

“Why would we compete with a $6B giant?” That was the question I asked Erik Dahl and Julia Hudea asking when we started Parrot (YC F25) . So before building, we interviewed 186 Duolingo users to understand what they loved, what kept them coming back, and where they still felt stuck. The pattern was surprisingly clear: people loved the streaks, the ease, and the fun - but many still didn’t feel like they could understand real people speaking. That became the bet behind Parrot: make learning languages feel as natural and addictive as scrolling TikTok, but built around real native videos and comprehensible input. ---- 1. We've helped hundreds of people replace some of their scrolling habits with the dream to learn a second language, and actually speak it 2. We've tripled our 2025 revenue and on track to 7x by the end of the year 3. We're hiring for our founding engineer position (link in the comments) 4. Grown to over 400K users 5.
